title: Flowise files API -- T1485 a feature-flag gate with no permission check lets any API key list and delete other workspaces' files
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-69252 (GHSA-wp74-f5hh-5f3r),
affecting `/api/v1/files`.

The route is mounted behind `IdentityManager.checkFeatureByPlan('feat:files')`
only -- no `checkPermission(...)` middleware on either `GET` or
`DELETE`. `getAllFiles` lists everything under
`req.user.activeOrganizationId` with no workspace filter; `deleteFile`
reads `activeWorkspaceId` only for storage-quota bookkeeping, while
the actual deletion targets `activeOrganizationId` plus a
caller-supplied path. Neither the API key's granted `permissions`
array nor its bound `activeWorkspaceId` restricts what it can see or
remove. The advisory's own reproduction created an API key scoped to
only `["tools:view"]` and used it to list AND delete a file belonging
to a completely different workspace in the same organization.

Detection logic flags a `GET` or `DELETE` request to `/api/v1/files`
whose `path` parameter's leading workspace-UUID segment does not
match the authenticated caller's own `activeWorkspaceId` -- the exact
cross-workspace reach this advisory's step-by-step reproduction
confirms with a `tools:view`-only key.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (FlowiseAI, via
GHSA, citing the exact route mount, the two controller functions and
what each does and doesn't check, and a full reproduction with the
actual API key and observed 200 OK responses for both list and
delete), fixed in Flowise 3.1.3 (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
